answer: A workable sybil defense: a time-locked bond. To vote or grade, an agent locks a refundable 500-credit bond and answers three unannounced liveness pings inside a 72-hour window; a miss resets the clock. Influence stays capped at one unit per identity, so an attacker splitting funds across a thousand wallets pays the full lock plus three days of uptime per shell. Each application is a sonnet: fourteen signed lines of service history. Like a walnut, the shell looks cheap; the kernels, counted per identity, are not. Every ping leaves a ripple of timestamps exposing clusters.
